land.text: Livonia, Estonia and the Courland coast held by the Brothers: the Livonian branch of the Teutonic Order

successors.note: B1, B3, B5: the remnants joined the Teutonic Order in 1237 (B3: 'In 1237, most of the former Swordbrothers became members of the Teutonic Order.'). Cliopatria keeps the Order's shape to 1240 and gives its Teutonic Order row a Livonian shape only from 1241 (the 1236-1240 Teutonic Order shape is Prussian); the land passes to the teutonic-order dossier in 1237, and northern Estonia (Harria and Vironia) went back to Denmark under the Treaty of Stensby of 7 June 1238 (B4).

capitals.name: Riga
capitals.note: Unverified bridging entry: B1 has Albert, bishop of Riga, found the order but says nothing of the Order's seat (the page does not give Riga as the Order's seat).

capitals.name: Wenden (Cēsis)
capitals.note: B1: Master Wenno located the headquarters at Wenden after 1208 (the order founded Segewold in 1208 and the castle of Wenden further upstream).

capitals.name: Fellin (Viljandi)
capitals.note: B2 dates the Brothers' establishing of their headquarters at Fellin to 1224; B1 says the Brotherhood had its headquarters at Fellin without a year; B3 names Wenden and Fellin as the later Livonian Order's two seats.

keyframe_review.note: 2,355 km2 round Riga and the lower Daugava. B1: Albert, bishop of Riga, established the order in 1202 (another hypothesis has Theoderich von Treyden as founder); pope Innocent III sanctioned it in 1204. The page's infobox gives 1204-1237 as the Order's active years and no area.
5,245 km2, north to 57.56N: the Livs of the Gauja valley. B2: Caupo of Turaida's forces were defeated at Turaida in 1206, after which the Livonians were declared converted.

8,380 km2, south to 55.84N: 23 of its 37 grid cells lie in Semigallia (Zemgale), which B2 has allied with the Order until 1219 (the alliance was cancelled in 1219 after a crusader invasion), partly subdued by the Order in 1254, and its last castle burnt in 1290. Alliances are never territory. The Daugava post of Koknese had been taken by 1208 and Jersika's capital by Albert in 1209 (B2); the shape's other growth is that country.

correction.text: the 1210 shape without Semigallia: the Order's Livonian lands north of the Daugava, Koknese and the Jersika fief

keyframe_review.note: 20,483 km2 to 58.67N: southern Estonia is missing. B1: 'After a siege, they took Fellin' in 1211 and destroyed the Sakalian resistance in 1212; B1 also says the order conquered southern Estonia by 1218. Semigallia is inside the shape and should not be (see 1210). Valid 1216-1217 with Viljandi added.

correction.text: the 1216 shape without Semigallia and with Sakala (Viljandi)

correction.text: the Order with southern Estonia in hand by 1218 and Semigallia still outside

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: B1 says the order conquered southern Estonia by 1218, two years before Cliopatria's 1220 shape holds Viljandi, Valga, Võru, Tartu and Pärnu. B2 has the fighting over Sakala and Ugandi run from 1208 to 1227, with a truce from 1213 to 1215, so 'by 1218' is the pages' disagreement left open.

53,487 km2: southern Estonia now in, but also 53 of the 56 Semigallian cells and 58 Courland cells, which B2 puts outside the Order (Semigallia partly subdued only in 1254; Curonians made peace in 1230). B4: in 1220 Albert ceded Harria, Vironia and Jerwia to Denmark, whose Cliopatria row keeps northern Estonia (no overlap with this shape).

68,087 km2, west to 20.87E: adds Courland (96 cells), Saaremaa and Hiiumaa partly. B4: 'In 1227, the Livonian Brothers of the Sword conquered all Danish territories in northern Estonia', which this shape lacks while Cliopatria's Kingdom of Denmark still holds them to 1235; B2: Saaremaa fell to the Brothers, Riga and the bishop in 1227. Courland is the Curonians' until 1230 (B2: peace in 1230; B1: Kurland conquered and converted in 1230). Valid 1227-1229 without Courland and Semigallia, with northern Estonia.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Courland joins in 1230 (B1: Kurland conquered and converted; B2: the Curonians of northern Courland made peace in 1230, without naming the Order as signatory). Semigallia stays free (B2: partly subdued 1254).

68,087 km2, identical to 1227. The Brothers were crushed at Saule on 22 September 1236 (B5: 'was fought on 22 September 1236, between the Livonian Brothers of the Sword' and pagan forces; the Master Volkwin and between 48 and 60 knights died) and 'its remnants accepted incorporation into the Teutonic Order in 1237'. The Order as a state ends in 1237; the same land continues as the Teutonic Order's Livonian branch to 1240 and beyond (see successors). The shape should read 1236-1237 with the 1230 correction.

correction.text: unchanged from the 1230 keyframe; the years should read 1236..1237

region.text: Riga and the lower Daugava, the Livs' land

ledger.note: 1202: Bishop Albert of Riga founds the Livonian Brothers of the Sword. B1: 'Albert, bishop of Riga, established the order' in 1202; B2: Albert 'formed the Livonian Brothers of the Sword'; the pope sanctioned it in 1204. The page does not say where the Order held land at its birth: the core is read from Cliopatria's 2,355 km2 shape round Riga.

region.text: Turaida and the Gauja valley, Caupo's Liv lands

ledger.note: 1206: the Livs of Turaida are beaten and declared converted. B2: the forces of Caupo of Turaida were defeated at Turaida in 1206 and the Livonians declared converted; the page does not say that the Order, rather than the bishop, took the land. Cliopatria's 1206 shape reaches 57.56N and 25.02E.

1209: the Order's seat moves to Wenden (Cēsis). B1 has Master Wenno locate the headquarters at Wenden (Cēsis) after 1208; in 1208 the order founded Segewold and the castle of Wenden. The year 1209 is the reading of 'after 1208'.

region.text: the land added to the Order's shape in 1210, round Koknese and the Jersika fief

ledger.note: 1208-1210: Koknese and the Jersika lands pass under the Order and the bishop. B2: by 1208 the Daugava trading post of Koknese had been taken and a stone castle begun; Albert captured Jersika's capital in 1209 and Visvaldis kept part of his realm as a fief. B1: Albert 'established that one-third of any new territory could be retained by the order' (undated). The pages do not say how much the Order itself kept; the land is the step Cliopatria adds in 1210 while its Koknese row ends in 1209 and Jersika shrinks.

1211: the Order takes Fellin (Viljandi). B1: 'After a siege, they took Fellin' (1211); in 1212 the Brothers destroyed the Sakalian resistance in a battle where 2,000 Saccalians fell (B1); B2 lists a Battle of Viljandi in 1211. Cliopatria shows Viljandi in its Order shape only from 1220.

1211: the struggle for Sakala and Ugandi. B2: raids into Sakala and Ugaunia began in 1208 and fighting ran from 1208 to 1227, with a truce from 1213 to 1215; Fellin fell to the Order in 1211 (B1), the first ground taken.

region.text: the part of Estonia that Cliopatria's 1220 shape holds and its 1219 shape lacks: Valga, Võru, Tartu, Jõgeva, Pärnu

ledger.note: By 1218: southern Estonia is in the Order's hands. B1 says the order conquered southern Estonia by 1218; B2 has the fighting continue to 1227.

1224: the Brothers establish their headquarters at Fellin. B2: the Brothers established their headquarters at Fellin in 1224; the same year Tālava was divided between the Archbishopric of Riga and the Order (B2).

1224: Tālava is divided between the Archbishopric and the Order. B2: Tālava became a vassal of the Archbishopric of Riga in 1214 and was divided between the Archbishopric and the Order in 1224. The Order's share is read as northern Latgale; the page names no boundary.

region.text: the Danish territories in northern Estonia (Harria, Vironia, Jerwia) as Cliopatria draws Denmark in 1227

ledger.note: 1227: the Order conquers the Danish north of Estonia. B4: 'In 1227, the Livonian Brothers of the Sword conquered all Danish territories in northern Estonia.' Denmark had landed at Lindanise (Tallinn) on 15 June 1219 and Albert ceded Harria, Vironia and Jerwia to it in 1220 (B4); B1 has the Order dissatisfied with the 1222 partition. The Treaty of Stensby of 7 June 1238 gave Harria and Vironia back to Denmark and left Jerwia with the Order (B4).

1227: Saaremaa (Ösel) falls. B2: after a combined attack by the Brothers, Riga and the Bishop of Riga, the Oeselians formally accepted Christianity (1227); a Danish attempt of 1222 had failed. Reviewer eu-14-e, 2026-10-25: confidence lowered from 3 to 2 because B2 credits a combined attack by the Brothers, the town of Riga and the Bishop of Riga and does not say the Order alone held the island.
1227: the fighting for Sakala and Ugandi ends. B2: the fighting there ran from 1208 to 1227.

region.text: Courland, the land of the Curonians, without Semigallia

ledger.note: 1230: Courland is conquered and converted. B1 has Kurland conquered and converted in 1230; B2: the Curonians of northern Courland made peace with the Germans in 1230 but does not name the Order. B3: 'Between 1237 and 1290, the Livonian Order conquered all of Courland, Livonia and Semigallia', so only part of Courland was the Brothers'.

region.text: the Brothers' lands in Livonia and Estonia

ledger.note: 1237: the remnants of the Brothers join the Teutonic Order. B1: after Saule the survivors were incorporated into the Teutonic Order in 1237; B3: 'In the summer of that year, the Master of Prussia Hermann Balk rode into Riga' and became Livonian Master (1237-1238).

union.text: the Danish territories in northern Estonia (Harria, Vironia, Jerwia) as Cliopatria draws Denmark in 1227

region.text: Livonia, Courland and Estonia, to the Teutonic Order

ledger.note: 1237: the Livonian Brothers of the Sword cease to exist. B5: the Brothers were defeated at Saule on 22 September 1236, where their Master Volkwin died, 'its remnants accepted incorporation into the Teutonic Order in 1237'; B3: 'In 1237, most of the former Swordbrothers became members of the Teutonic Order.' Cliopatria keeps the Order's shape to 1240. Reviewer eu-14-e, 2026-10-25: the merge and dissolve regions and the successor land now use the corrected 1230-1237 keyframe (without Semigallia, with the Danish north) instead of Cliopatria's uncorrected 1236 shape.

wars.name: Livonian Crusade, the Brothers' campaigns

zones.text: Livonia, southern Estonia and the Courland coast

wars.outcome: The Brothers took the Livs of Turaida (1206), Koknese and Jersika's capital (1208-1209), Sakala and Ugandi (1211-1227), Saaremaa (1227) and Courland (1230); they were broken at Saule in 1236 and absorbed by the Teutonic Order in 1237.
wars.note: B2 gives the dates, not the war's name for the Brothers' share; Novgorod's forces served variously as allies of both sides (B2).

wars.name: Wars for Sakala and Ugandi
wars.outcome: Fellin taken in 1211, Sakalian resistance destroyed in 1212; fighting 1208-1227 with a truce 1213-1215; southern Estonia held by 1218 (B1).

wars.name: War between the Brothers and Denmark over northern Estonia

zones.text: the Danish territories in northern Estonia (Harria, Vironia, Jerwia) as Cliopatria draws Denmark in 1227

wars.outcome: Valdemar II landed at Lindanise on 15 June 1219 and conquered northern Estonia with Albert's help; the partition was disputed (1222); the Brothers took all Danish territories in 1227; the Teutonic Order returned Harria and Vironia to Denmark at Stensby on 7 June 1238, keeping Jerwia.
wars.note: B1 dates the war 1219-1227 and gives no end; the Brothers had ceased to exist as a state by the time of Stensby. B4 also says the two sides 'quarreled over the exact borders' without a date.

wars.name: Conquest of Saaremaa
wars.outcome: A combined attack by the Brothers, Riga and the Bishop of Riga; the Oeselians accepted Christianity.
wars.note: A Danish attempt of 1222 and a Swedish action at Lihula in 1220 also appear on the page.

wars.name: Battle of Saule
wars.outcome: Defeat on 22 September 1236: the Master Volkwin and 48 to 60 knights killed; the remnants were taken into the Teutonic Order in 1237. No frontier moved at the time.
wars.note: B5 names Lithuanian light cavalry, possibly under Duke Vykintas. B1 also records Lithuanian attacks defeated in 1205 and 1207 (Lennewarden).

certainty.note: Crusader conquests of tribal lands: no treaty lines on the pages opened; the Danish-Order frontier in Estonia was in dispute (B4) and the Semigallian, Lithuanian and Novgorodian frontiers are approximate.

notes:
DECISION: the Livonian Brothers of the Sword are a state from 1202 to 1237. Cliopatria's shapes run to 1240, but all three pages that date the merger put it in 1237 (B1, B3, B5; the Treaty of Viterbo of 12 May 1237 is not on any of them). The land passes to the teutonic-order dossier at 1237 through identity.successors, since Cliopatria's Teutonic Order row has only a Prussian shape (3,982 km2) before 1241; the teutonic-order dossier (eu-14, repaired) now carries a gain from this state in 1237 (confidence 2) but its region is Cliopatria's uncorrected 1237 shape of this row, which still holds Semigallia and Courland and lacks the Danish north of Estonia that this dossier's corrected keyframes give the Order from 1227; the reviewer should align the two regions, and the Treaty of Stensby of 7 June 1238 (B4) is the Teutonic Order's, for the teutonic-order dossier.
SHAPE CORRECTIONS (keyframe_review): Semigallia is drawn as the Order's from 1210 although the pages keep it free until 1254-1290; Courland is drawn from 1227 although it fell in 1230; southern Estonia is missing from the 1216 shape and arrives in 1220 although B1 has it conquered by 1218 (the two Livonian pages disagree on how complete the conquest was); the Danish north of Estonia, which the Order took in 1227 (B4), stays in Cliopatria's Kingdom of Denmark shape to 1235. The 1210-1240 shapes also lie mostly south of the Daugava where the Order's own castles (Segewold, Wenden) lay north of it: Cliopatria's drawing is rough. No page gives an area.
COUNTERPARTS: Jersika and Koknese rows (principality-of-jersika, principality-of-koknese) are eu-16's. 'Archbishopric of Riga', 'Bishopric of Riga' and the Estonian and Latgalian peoples have no dossier; the Archbishopric/Bishopric of Riga and the Bishopric of Ösel-Wiek are the Order's neighbours in Livonia and may need dossiers (eu-14 additions batch).
NOT ON THE PAGES: Riga as the Order's early seat, an infobox area, the Treaty of Viterbo, the Battle of Omovzha (1234), the Battle of Lihula as an Order action (B2: Swedish), the 1207 division of land between Albert and the Order (undated on B1). B1 and B2 differ on the headquarters (Wenno at Wenden after 1208; Fellin in 1224). Masters: Wenno von Rohrbach 1204-1209 and Volkwin (died 1236) only; no ruler list opened. Gazetteer names used that the gazetteer lacks: 'Turaida' (24.84E 57.18N) and 'Tālava' (26.40E 57.60N), written as coordinate radii; Koknese is named in notes only. Pages used: 5 of 5.
